children: Dell Technologies’ (DELL) revenue doubled after booking over $60 billion in new AI orders last quarter, and the company raised its full-year forecasts, sending a clear message that the AI server demand remains robust.
Still,
moved up a mere 1% in overnight trading following the report.

At a time when investors worry AI infrastructure spending is nearing a peak, Dell management pushed back, arguing the supply-demand deficit will get worse next year and praising the quality of its AI orders.
Dell Says Its $132B AI Backlog Is ‘Fully Vetted’

“Behind every customer engagement in every order is a rigorous due diligence process resulting in a fully vetted backlog. Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power,” COO Jeffrey Clarke said on the analyst call.
"We've had no customers rescheduled business. The backlog continues to be very firm,” he said, adding that the company remains “highly selective” in terms of neocloud customers.

Dell ended Q3 with a record AI server backlog of $132.3 billion after booking $60.2 billion in new orders during the quarter. The company highlighted that Nvidia Vera Rubin-NVL72 were driving the bulk of the new orders.
AI Servers Are Taking Priority Over PCs
After Intel’s warnings about the PC market earlier this month, Dell admitted that the segment was soft and that it was prioritizing its server business based on customer trends.
"Customers are prioritizing their budgets near term to servers and storage, electing to defer some PC-related refresh," Clarke said.
"I think companies are deferring their PC purchases to ensure they have the infrastructure to work in what is going to be a very disruptive era with agentic technology, really reinventing companies."
Notably, Dell said it is actively prioritizing its Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) over PCs, even reallocating silicon supply from Client Solutions Group (CSG) to build more servers.
Dell’s Q3 Earnings Snapshot
Dell’s October quarter revenue
103% to $54.9 billion, beating expectations of $49.3 billion. Adjusted profit was $9.45 per share, also well above the target of $6.60.

Dell's ISG revenue jumped 198% to $42 billion, with sales of AI-optimized servers surging 291% to $22 billion. Sales in the CSG segment, which houses commercial and consumer PCs, increased a mere 3% to $12.9 billion.
Dell now expects fiscal-year adjusted earnings of $29.68 a share on $202 billion of revenue. It previously guided for adjusted earnings of $25.50 a share on revenue of $192 billion.
The report shows that PC market is weak across the board, Patrick Moorhead, chief analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said in an X post.
“$INTC lost 29% the day after it put numbers on the PC downturn. Four prints later, all four confirmed it,” flagging inputs from Advanced Micro Devices, Lenovo, Hewlett Packard, and now Dell.
“Good news is that demand is deferred, not destroyed. Nobody rides a five-year-old PC another five years. Memory will decide the timing,” he said.
CNBC’s Jim Cramer said: “Dell should be higher. I liked the Nvidia situation,” referring to the muted stock move.
Retail View For DELL
On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for DELL increased multiple points higher in the ‘extremely bullish’ zone, with several traders questioning the dull stock reaction.
“$DELL the market has lost its mind , this now has a 7 forward PE. But let’s give Walmart a 47 forward PE and every cyber security stock in existence a 100 PE. This market is straight up rigged,”
a trader.
Another said: “$DELL lol this should be up 10-20%, this market is a joke.”
“Correction day overall, gains have not been erased so it ends on a positive,” said a trader. “Dell is not Intel, Dell is not HPE - Trump himself has a stake on DELL.”
DELL shares hit an all-time high in October and have dipped over 40% since then, in line with a broader selloff in AI-linked stocks. Year to date, the stock remains 137% higher.
Dell reported Q3 results above expectations and raised its fiscal 2027 forecasts.
Like Intel, Dell flagged softness in the PC market and said it is prioritizing its server business.
Retail sentiment for DELL increased multiple points higher in the ‘extremely bullish’ zone.

title: Dell Says AI Demand Remains ‘Firm,’ Every Order ‘Fully Vetted’ – But DELL Stock Barely Moves After Beat-And-Raise Quarter
